public_rationale: The condition is not established. Federal Reserve analysis reports growing adoption through November 2025, while a July 2026 consumer survey reports declining frequent chatbot use. These measures do not settle whether broad AI usage fell. CBRE's low vacancy figure is context, not a test of what happened after such a decline. Under the conditional-forecast rule, an unknown antecedent makes this claim not adjudicable at the cutoff. That does not mean the forecast is false. Its consequences also have no clear deadline, and the revenue accounting basis is unspecified.
limitations: A narrower reading of usage could treat the consumer survey as evidence that the condition occurred.
Adoption, usage intensity, leased-space vacancy, and computing utilization are different measures.
The available records do not establish the full conditional sequence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Once AI usage drops, the remarkable amounts of revenue that have flowed into big tech will drop too, and acres of data centers will sit unused.

statement.excerpt: Once usage drops, so will the remarkable amounts of revenue that have flowed into big tech, and so will acres of data centers sit unused, the cloud equivalent of the massive overhiring we saw in post-lockdown Silicon Valley.

from_speaker: so will the remarkable amounts of revenue that have flowed into big tech
acres of data centers sit unused
our_interpretation: I read usage as actual generative-AI use across the market. A temporary decline at one service does not by itself establish the condition.
I read the revenue consequence as a decline in big tech's AI-related revenue, and the capacity consequence as substantial completed data-center space becoming idle following that usage decline.
The claim requires both consequences. Slower revenue growth is not a revenue decline, and canceled construction is not completed capacity sitting unused.
The adjacent reference to three quarters concerns the predicted apocalypse. It does not clearly specify a deadline for completing this conditional sequence, so I leave its horizon open.
No accounting basis is stated or implied by an attributed financial figure. I therefore record it as unknown.
criteria.support_condition: A documented broad decline in generative-AI usage is followed by both lower comparable AI-related revenue across big tech and substantial completed data-center capacity becoming unused.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a documented broad usage decline, comparable revenue and facility records establish that at least one promised consequence did not occur over the resulting contraction episode. Brief continued growth cannot conclusively contradict a forecast with no specified response lag.

evidence.excerpt: The most recent quarter saw the strongest growth in work-related adoption over the course of the RPS series.
evidence.locator: Estimated AI Adoption Rates, paragraph discussing the November 2025 Real-Time Population Survey
evidence.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence.explanation: The analysis reports rising work-related and non-work generative-AI adoption through November 2025. It does not establish the triggering decline, but adoption shares cannot exclude falling usage intensity or a later contraction.

evidence.excerpt: That suggests more and more people are taking against the very idea of AI
evidence.locator: Regular AI usage, paragraph discussing respondents who do not use chatbots
evidence.explanation: The report describes a 1,008-person survey in which several-times-daily chatbot use fell relative to the previous year and non-use increased. This supports a narrower consumer decline, but does not establish a broad contraction including enterprise and API usage; survey field dates and sufficient sampling details are absent.

evidence.excerpt: Vacancy held steady at 1.4% compared with year-end 2025.
evidence.locator: Paragraph reporting primary-market supply, net absorption, and vacancy
evidence.explanation: CBRE reports low vacancy in eight primary North American data-center markets for the first half of 2026. This measures market vacancy rather than global AI computing utilization and is not evidence about capacity following an established usage contraction.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented broad usage contraction, followed by comparable AI-related realized revenue records and evidence of substantial completed capacity becoming idle. A negative verdict would also require a defensible response window; continued growth before the antecedent occurs cannot refute the claim.
